#753. Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford

Gino Pozzo (left) has presided over 25 permanent Watford bosses in 14 years, with Alessio Dionisi the latest to take charge of the Hornets

A week is said to be a long time in football, and few clubs offer a more compelling test of that theory than Watford.

It has been 14 years since the Pozzo family completed their takeover of the Hornets and Alessio Dionisi's dismissal leaves them searching for the 25th permanent boss of their tenure.

The Italian's dismissal was announced on Sunday lunchtime with his 18th and final game in charge proving to be the 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United less than 24 hours earlier.

An average incumbency of about 210 days per manager has generated all too familiar headlines of the Hornets seeking a new face in the dugout, but is there method in the madness?

Pozzo court case in Spain adds to unrest at Watford

Brereton Diaz double leads Blades to win over Watford

The Hornets were taken over by the Pozzos on 29 June 2012, with the family having also owned Serie A side Udinese since 1986.

Gino Pozzo has been in charge ever since, overseeing an ownership model rooted in a vast global scouting network famed for buying low and selling high, with Brazil internationals Richarlison and Joao Pedro among those flipped for big fees.

In the 61-year-old's first seven years, the club shifted from existential crisis to FA Cup finalists.

Under Javi Gracia, they came close to qualifying for Europe through the Premier League in 2019 before arriving at a Wembley showpiece where they came up second best to Manchester City.

But it proved to be a peak from which they have steadily spiralled.

Relegation from the Premier League a year later was followed by an immediate return - but a further relegation from which they have not recovered.

Last season's 16th-place finish was their lowest in the second tier under Pozzo - with a frequent turnover of manager seemingly utilised as a failed antidote to their stagnation.

That sense of inertia - and a poor start to 2026-27 which has left them 21st in the Championship, has brightened the spotlight on the owner and his methods.

With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone

After back-to-back hammerings by Burnley and Cardiff City in October, former Hornets midfielder Tom Ince said he feared for the club he left at the end of last season.

"There are a lot of different beliefs on how the football club should move forward." Ince told the 72+ podcast.

He pointed to Gracia ending his second spell in charge last season after only three months - and with the club four points off the Championship play-offs - as a "big, big problem" that summed up their instability.

"There is so much control away from the manager at that club that it will always be an issue," said Ince. "The players don't see the manager as the focal point. He [Pozzo] is the one in control.

"That is always going to be a problem because you can't look at a manager and not have any fear [in them].

"I look at Watford, the players in the dressing room. You have a lot of young players, who have not played in England before. When this hiring and firing of managers is going on, they're just like 'OK, onto the next one [manager]'."

While Ince, now at League Two side Tranmere Rovers, added his respect for positives to Pozzo's practise, he is not alone in speaking out about the board's influence.

Speaking on No Tippy Tappy Football,, external former England boss Sam Allardyce said he had turned down the chance to manage the club prior to the appointment of Nigel Pearson in 2019.

"I got interviewed at Watford before Nigel [Pearson]," Allardyce revealed.

"[Sir] Elton [John] rang me up and said, 'Come on, Sam, take the job'.

"It was very nice having a phone call from Elton John, I must admit. But I met with the board, sat in the boardroom, and went, 'I can't take this job'.

"They were telling me what to do, saying, 'Play this way, play that player, this manager's not been playing that player' and so on."

Gino Pozzo has been Watford's owner since 2012

Ince and Allardyce's remarks came after former Watford owner John said he was "upset and disappointed" by the club's form after their 4-0 defeat by Burnley.

"I really feel for the supporters who have to watch this," he wrote in response to a club post on Instagram.

When supporter group The 1881 Movement published an open letter declaring a "complete loss of confidence" in Pozzo, the Italian, who has rarely spoken publically had no choice but to.

His meeting with prominent supporter Roy Moore was recorded and released as an extraordinary 114-minute podcast episode by the club's official channels.

Watford fans state 'loss of confidence' in ownership

Elton John 'upset and disappointed' with Watford form

"I don't have a social presence, I don't like to speak publicly, I don't enjoy that, I don't think it's productive for the work we do," Pozzo explained.

"I don't like to answer to speculation, because a lot of the people that are out there want a bit of visibility for themselves. Unfortunately social media creates this sort of character.

"I'm not expecting everybody to understand our model. In order to compete with the other clubs, we need to be something different. Otherwise we would not even be in the Championship right now."

Though Udinese is formally owned by his father, Giampaolo, Pozzo is still heavily involved in the management of the Italian club.

It is for this reason that he dismisses a reputation for devouring head coaches - Udinese boss Kosta Runjaic was, until his sacking earlier this month,, external Serie A's longest-serving manager having been appointed before the 2024-25 season.

"I tend to have a very good relationship with the coach, because the coach is a fundamental part," said Pozzo. "Whenever we sign a coach there is normally strong bond and good idea and we share that.

"It [sacking managers] has cost me a lot, I know I'm not looking good. Every time I change a coach, it's not a good image. But I cannot stand the fact that my image is worth more than the club's results. I put the club in front."

Watford have finished outside the top 10 in each of their past four Championship seasons

Before the win over Charlton Athletic on 17 October, some supporters tried to orchestrate a protest against Pozzo's ownership.

It is a far cry from the high point of his reign, when a tifo bearing his name was unfurled at Vicarage Road.

Tom Bodell, a Hornets supporter who contributes to the Watford Buzz podcast, said outside views of the club being a "basket case" who change manager two or three times a season was "the tip of the iceberg".

"We've seen over certainly three years, possibly five years now, a real reduction in overheads and outlay on the football side," he said.

"This summer we saw quite a bit of talent leave for reasonable money and next to nothing spent. We paid a fee for the goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia, but I believe that was it.

"Everybody else was either a loan, a free transfer or came from Udinese. So, you know, passing money from one pocket to the other on the same pair of jeans."

Bodell said chief executive and chairman Scott Duxbury had failed to deliver on promises of signing players with proven EFL experience, with concerns also mounting over the downgrading of the club's academy.

"There have been enough instances now of supporters feeling that they've been at best let down, at worst kind of misled or lied to that it is very hard to rebuild that trust," said Bodell.

"They [the owners] are at very real risk of leaving us in a worse position than when they arrived and I think that is probably the thing that has tipped people into action."

Alessio Dionisi lost more than half of his games in charge of Watford

But while the optics of Pozzo's model and methods have hit an all-time low for English observers, his image in his homeland is assured, according to Vincenzo Credendino, a journalist with Sport Italia.

"The [Pozzo] business model is a winning model because he is not an American billionaire or an Arab Sultan, he has to apply the model he worked on to buy young players and sell them," said Credendino.

"This is a model that allows Gino Pozzo with Udinese to compete in the Champions League, and reaching high levels at least in Italian football.

"If you look at many teams in Serie A, you can find many players who came out from Udinese. Piotr Zielinski, at Inter Milan is just one example."

For the frustration of Hornets' fans, it is a point that is difficult to deny.

Rodrigo de Paul, Alexis Sanchez, Alex Meret and Juan Cuadrado are all examples of players bought low and sold high at Udinese.

While at Watford, Abdoulaye Doucoure and Odion Ighalo are further examples of players to bring money into the Hertfordshire club.

"When you speak about Gino Pozzo, you are speaking about a piece of history." added Credendino.

"He's really pioneering. He has visions of the future. He has agreed a new perspective about many things, and many clubs look at his model and decided to make something similar."

So, is there method in the madness? Undoubtedly. But for those associated with Watford, the madness alone might prove to be Pozzo's lasting legacy.

#752. Selena Gomez Reacts to Martin Short, Meryl Streep Romance Rumors

Selena Gomez cheekily reacted to Martin Short bringing up Meryl Streep in a conversation about Only Murders in the Building guest stars, two years after the pair sparked romance rumors.

Selena Gomez just proved you’re not the only one hoping for Meryl Streep and Martin Short romance.

During an Only Murders in the Building FYC event in Hollywood Nov. 19, Gomez cheekily jumped in while Short detailed his awe of working with Streep, as well as Jennifer Saunders and Olivia Coleman.

“I don’t know why Meryl keeps coming up,” Gomez joked to laughs from the audience as well as Short himself. “Finally, I get to reuse a joke. Yes!”

To which Short wiped his eyes adding, “I know.”

Earlier that same day, Gomez had made a similar joke while taping an episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live! alongside Short.

“I get so geeked out,” Gomez admitted of working alongside Streep. “We’ve worked together for a while.”

And when Short—whose wife Nancy Dolman died following a cancer battle in 2010—clarified it was Streep’s fourth season on Only Murders, Gomez quipped, “Yeah, I don’t know why she keeps coming back.”

Visibly taken aback, Short simply added, “Yeah, I don’t know either.”

Of course, romance rumors have been stirring between Short and Streep since 2024, when they appeared to be getting closer after Streep joined the series the year prior, particularly following a cozy night out at the Golden Globes.

But while the pair share an on-screen romance, a rep for Short confirmed to E! News at the time that the pair were “just very good friends” but “nothing more.”

Nevertheless, Short has admitted that even he was starstruck by working with the Devil Wears Prada alum—who announced she split from her husband Don Gummer in 2023.

“The first day of shooting with her, I was going to work, and—you know, I'm not new to show business,” Short told E! News in 2024. “I thought, ‘I am nervous today. Why?' Oh yeah, I'm working with Meryl.”

The Saturday Night Live alum was floored, however, when he learned that Streep felt the same.

"She said, ‘Okay, my nerves are to half,’” he recalled. “I went, ‘Oh, okay, that's pretty cool. Maybe that's why you're the greatest actress, because you've never taken anything for granted.’”

For more stars who never dated despite their on-screen chemistry sparking romance rumors, keep reading…

The Anyone But You costars may have found love onscreen, but that's where it stayed. Despite the onslaught of dating rumors amid their 2023 press tour, the pair emphasized that their relationship was strictly platonic.

"The two things that you have to sell a rom-com are fun and chemistry," Powell told the New York Times in April 2024. "Sydney and I have a ton of fun together, and we have a ton of effortless chemistry. That's people wanting what's on the screen off the screen, and sometimes you just have to lean into it a bit—and it worked wonderfully. Sydney is very smart."

Meanwhile, Sweeney—who was engaged to businessman Jonathan Davino at the time, though they split in March 2025 after seven years together—asserted that she and Powell didn't play up their chemistry ahead of the rom-com's release.

"Honestly, the press did it themselves. There was no leaning in, per se," she told Variety in October 2025. "Truly, the tabloids and journalists just created it and kept going."

"Glen and I genuinely care for each other and have a love and respect for one another," the actress emphasized. "I love being with him. And I think people just truly saw a really beautiful pairing."

Hermione Granger and Draco Malfoy?! If Watson had it her way, the Harry Potter franchise would have had a Hogwarts House-crossed romance going down off-screen. The actress has admitted to nursing a serious crush on her bleached blonde costar.During the Harry Potter 20th anniversary special, Watson shared that as a child she "fell in love" with Felton while on the set of their first film together, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. "I used to come in every day and look for his number on the call sheet, it was No. 7, and if his name was on the call sheet, it was an extra exciting day," she said during the reunion. "He was three years above me and so for him he was like, 'You're like my little sister.'"Shortly after the special premiered, fans of the series quickly took to the Internet to share their wish for the longtime friends to become something more.However, in an interview with British Vogue, Watson addressed the online reaction and put any potential dating rumors to rest. "We speak most weeks," she said, "and we just think it's sweet."

The one where Ross and Rachel were almost each other's lobsters in real-life.During HBO Max's Friends reunion, Aniston and Schwimmer—who played one of TV's most beloved couples—explained that art reflected real life a bit during the show's first season. "At some point, we were both crushing hard on each other, but it was like two ships passing because one of us was always in a relationship, and we never crossed that boundary," Schwimmer said. "We respected that."Aniston added, "Honestly, I remember saying one time to David, 'It's going to be such a bummer if the first time you and I actually kiss is going to be on national television.' And sure enough, the first time we kissed was in that coffee shop."So, instead of having a romance IRL, she explained that they "just channeled all of our adoration and love for each other into Ross and Rachel."

Arguably one of the most iconic pairings in movie history, fans have shipped Leo and Kate together since 1996's Titanic (even though she didn't make room for him on that door). Still, they never let go of their friendship, with Winslet telling The Guardian that they are "bonded for life." From walking the red carpet together at the 1998 Golden Globes to watching DiCaprio blow kisses to Winslet during her emotional 2009 Golden Globes speech, it's so evident that the feelings between the besties have only continued to grow over the past two decades, iceberg be damned.

The unexpected pairing's chemistry in 2019's A Star Is Born and its ensuing press tour made fans blind to the fact that the actor was dating Irina Shayk and the "Bad Romance" singer was engaged to Christian Carano at the time.Still, it was clear that the costars had a close bond, with Gaga revealing that she had an "instant connection" with Cooper that came "the second that I saw him."Of course, that closeness was on full display when the pair took to the Oscars stage in 2019, hand-in-hand, to perform their Best Song-winning number, "Shallow," just days after Gaga ended her engagement.

But the House of Gucci star quickly shut down romance rumors following the performance, telling Jimmy Kimmel, "Yes, people saw love and—guess what—that's what we wanted you to see."Cooper, whose romance with Shayk ended later that year, never addressed the speculation until November 2021, telling The Hollywood Reporter they were acting during the Oscar performance."They kind of fall in love in that scene in the film," he explained. "It's that explosive moment that happens to them on a stage in front of thousands of people…It would have been so weird if we were both on stools facing the audience."

Gaga isn't the first costar Cooper has been romantically linked to in the press, with his onscreen dynamic with Lawrence in movies such as Silver Linings Playbook and American Hustle sparking rumors for years. In fact, Cooper was asked by Howard Stern in 2015, "When are you two gonna have sex? Everyone is waiting for that." The actor was quick to respond, "Never. It's just not the way we are together."And, at the 2013 Golden Globes, when he was asked by Entertainment Tonight if they were were dating, Cooper responded, "Oh my god. That's very funny. No, my God, no."

Since starring in Speed together in 1994, rumors have raced over the decades that Bullock and Reeves had an off-screen romance. Alas, it was never meant to me, with Sandra denying the two were ever a couple in an interview with Esquire magazine."Nope...but who knows?," she said. "Keanu's a guy who, I feel like, is friends with every woman he's ever dated. I don't think there's anyone who has something horrible to say about him. So maybe we could have survived. I don't know. But we didn't have to survive anything. We just get to grow up together on parallel roads and tip our hats and meet for a dinner and try to work together. And the longer time goes on, the more in awe I am of the human being. Would I have been able to say that if he had dumped me and made me angry? Probably not."Still, the duo, who also costarred in 2006's The Lake House, are close friends, with Bullock citing Reeves's listening skills as one of his best attributes. The Miss Congeniality star recalled that about a year after filming Speed, she casually mentioned to her costar that she'd never had champagne and truffles. A few days later, she told the outlet, Reeves hand-delivered those two items (and flowers), explaining, "I just thought you might want to try champagne and truffles, to see what it's like."

Moviegoers have Crazy, Stupid, Love for this pairing after they've played romantic interests in three films, including La La Land.Though they never dated in real life, working together forged a bond between the two actors. During a Q&A session at the 2018 Telluride Film Festival, the Cruella star revealed how much Gosling meant to her and his impact on her life and career. Calling him a "dear, wonderful friend," Stone said, "I can't even imagine what my life would be without Ryan. She then added, "He's so special. It makes me emotional."And before La La Land debuted in 2016, Stone joked around about the number of films she's done with Gosling, telling E! News, "He has a restraining order against me now.""Restraining order" aside, Gosling said it was "great to work" with Emma, explaining, "I think it brings the best out of [us] because you know one another, and you are able to help each other in a way that you can't if you're strangers."

Jim and Pam on The Office are one of the most beloved TV couples of all-time, with fans rooting for the Dunder Mifflin employees to be together throughout the NBC hit's nine-year run. Jam's chemistry never transitioned into an off-screen romance between John and Jenna, though she did admit to the pair having "real chemistry" during a 2016 appearance on Watch What Happens Live when a caller asked how close they were."There's like a real part of me that is Pam and a real part of him that's Jim and those parts of us were genuinely in love with one another," Fischer explained. "But in real life we aren't totally Pam and totally Jim, so in real life we're not the perfect match…he was like a type of spouse that I had for a long time, he was my partner and we will always be close because of it."Krasinski later weighed in on his costar's headline-making comments, telling The Daily Beast, "I think we both feel it's such an honor to be a part of that relationship. As far as how she was quoted about saying we were 'genuinely in love,' I think that was taken wildly out of context and I feel bad for her."We'll always have the teapot.

They may have costarred in How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, but the pair gained a rapid number of fans rooting for them to find each other IRL after the 2006 rom-com. But it never happened.In an interview with Howard Stern on his SiriusXM show in October 2020, McConaughey revealed it simply never appealed to him to date one of his famous costars."I've always tried to keep it professional and the people I worked with, I must say, did it well," he shared. "Maybe we had certain crushes on each other at certain times but we always just kept it professional."

And with that, the chance for their love to blossom died, just like that love fern.

These A-list best friends have off-the-charts on-screen chemistry (Ocean's Eleven, anyone?) that has extended offscreen in a purely platonic way. Just look at their giggle-filled interviews, gushing public speeches and the fact that George has lent out his coveted Lake Como home to the Roberts-Moder family for anniversary celebrations. NBD!

Along with the ball dropping on New Year's Eve, you can always count on people wondering if the best friends and CNN's Live From Times Square co-hosts have ever dated. When Cohen appeared on Howard Stern's radio show, he was asked, "What is it about Anderson Cooper that keeps you from falling in love with him?" The Watch What Happens Live host replied, "I just think it's not what our relationship is based on. We're just friends. That's not a part of it. I think, at this point, we know each other too well. We're not attracted to each other in that way."Funnily enough, the pair first met when they were set up on a blind date over 25 years ago. "You know when straight people know two gay guys, they're like, 'Oh, you guys should meet,'" Cooper said on The Tonight Show in 2017, adding that when the two had a phone call to schedule the date, he "knew within 45 seconds I was never going on a date with Andy Cohen."He explained that Cohen "violated" a cardinal rule" when it comes to dating the CNN host: He asked about Anderson's mother, Gloria Vanderbilt. "I wanted to date the Vanderbilt boy!" Cohen admitted. "I was excited!"

While Deschanel said the pair had "so much fun" making the 2009 indie rom-com (500) Days of Summer, Gordon-Levitt admitted dating his costar and longtime friend would be "awkward" in a 2012 interview with Playboy."Zooey and I just think it's funny," he said of fans wanting them to be together. "It is funny. We've been friends for 10 years."

Before it was confirmed that the High School Musical heartthrob was dating his costar Vanessa Hudgens, there was speculation that he was involved with their mutual best friend Tisdale. His 2006 guest appearance as her love interest on The Suite Life of Zack and Cody only fueled the rumors.Efron and Tisdale still remain close to this day, with the latter calling him her "brother/best friend," though she did pick him as her worst onscreen kiss in an interview with Elle. "It was the worst because he is like my brother," Tisdale explained. "At the time, he was used to acting on Warner Brothers, which is CW, and we were on Disney Channel."She then called him out for trying to kiss her "with his tongue," prompting her to tell him, "'Get away from me!'""I closed my mouth so fast. I was like, 'This is Disney Channel, we don't kiss like that on Disney Channel!'" Tisdale recalled. "It's just weird when you're so close to somebody, we'd already done a movie, I'd known him for years before,'" she said. "'That is why it was the worst, it's just we're too close.'"

While their High School Musical characters Chad and Taylor were teen sweethearts, Bleu and Coleman left the Disney franchise with a lifelong friendship. The duo reunited onscreen in the 2021 Lifetime Christmas movie, A Christmas Dance Reunion, with Bleu writing on Instagram, "After 13 years it felt like coming home working and dancing with [Monique] again. Starring in a [Lifetime] Christmas movie has always been a dream of mine, but never in a million years did I think I'd get to share the screen with one of my favorite people."And Coleman is hoping to continue working with "one of her best friends," telling People, "I honestly pray that we get to do more things together because we have that sort of spark that Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan had, and Leo and Kate, and Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, and all of these different couples that we've seen in movie after movie together. I really feel like we have that potential as well and I'd like to see that happen."

They may have played one of TV's most iconic will-they-or-won't-they couples on The X-Files, but the costars actually didn't get along while filming their hit Fox show. In a 2008 interview with Metro UK, Duchovny admitted that he often fought with Anderson during the series' initial eight-year run because, "Familiarity breeds contempt. It's nothing to do with the other person. We used to argue about nothing. We couldn't stand the sight of each other."That didn't stop fans from wanting Mulder and Scully to get together, both on-screen and off, with a photo from their May 2021 lunch date going viral, much to Duchovny's amusement. "As I was leaving she was like, 'Let's take a photo,'" he told People. "I was told there was a big reaction to it! I never get that stuff, but it's really cool that people are interested after all these years."

Avengers shippers, assemble!While they've appeared in nine movies together since first collaborating on 2004's The Perfect Score, the superhero costars have never hooked up IRL. But Evans and Johansson have developed a deep comfort level with each other over the years. "It's really a result of 10 years of knowing somebody," Johansson explained of their chemistry to Entertainment Weekly in March 2020, "and being able to have a kind of intimacy with them that I think you get from just spending a lot of time with somebody and knowing their soft underbelly."

#751. It’s our duty to promote ourselves: even to other scientists. Am I wrong?

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Recently, I submitted my faculty file to be considered for promotion. I thought that being elected as a fellow at one of the most prestigious research institutes in my field — bioethics — would strengthen my case. But it seemed that no one I spoke to at my university had heard of the fellowship, and the value of it wasn’t recognized.

I had an epiphany: if others don’t see the value, that’s on me. I need to better communicate why my work matters, rather than assuming that it speaks for itself.

So I withdrew my file and will resubmit it when I have developed a stronger argument for the significance of the fellowship, and will gather support from senior colleagues on its merit. I know my work is valued outside my own university sphere; now I must make that case internally.

If we want our work to count towards career advancement, it’s up to us to show our peers why it matters.

Am I wrong? — Brandon Brown, public-health and biomedical-ethics specialist at the University of California, Riverside.

“I couldn’t disagree more. I think it’s a shame that scientists need to almost beg their peers to see the value of our work. Most of us invest huge amounts of time, effort and funding into what we do because we genuinely believe it matters. If you truly think your own work is irrelevant unless you can ‘sell it’ to others, then perhaps you’re in the wrong profession.” — Juliana Sanchez Alponti Millar, biologist at the University of York, UK.

“The balancing act of spending your time doing what you think is important and convincing others about the value is tricky and always there — this is a good example of how you need your colleagues and mentors to understand your motivations and the ‘big plan’.’’ — Russ Altman, bioengineer and geneticist at Stanford University in California.

“I completely agree with this. As scientists, we often assume our work will speak for itself, but communication and visibility matter a lot. Many of us also lack marketing and self-promotion skills, even though they can make a huge difference in these situations.” — Mariana Belén Galeano, biologist at the University of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

“The beauty of science is that the scientific process itself sorts out which research is useful. Scientists should do science, publish it and, rather than spend time campaigning for their work, go back and do more science.” — Metin Eren, anthropologist and archaeologist at Kent State University in Kent, Ohio.

“Researchers do need to make their case, but they shouldn’t have to do it alone. Universities must do their part, too: set clear paths to promotion, review progress regularly and make sure managers explain to their staff members how promotion works.” — Timothy Davis, volcanologist at the University of Bristol, UK.

“We are our own best advocates. It’s taken me some time to shed the modesty and be comfortable with promoting my own work and accolades, but a friend once told me ‘no one cares as much about your career as you do,” and that stuck. You have to show people why they should care.’ — Margaret Swift, ecologist at Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability and Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine in Ithaca, New York.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02203-2

Responses have been edited for length and clarity.
